call_model.kernel: core/src/semantic/call.rs: CallDispatchKind (StaticResolved/DynamicResolvedSet/DynamicPartial/Unresolved -- the contract's exact vocabulary) and CallSiteIdentity { repository, revision, function: SemanticRecordId (the CALLER's FunctionIdentity record_id), span, dispatch, callees: Vec<SemanticRecordId> }.
call_model.identity_key_design: CallSiteIdentity::identity_key() deliberately excludes dispatch/callees -- only repository/revision/function/span participate. dispatch/callees are treated as a RESOLUTION FACT about an already-uniquely-identified call site (identified by caller + span), not an identity-disambiguating feature, so record_id stays stable if a later wave improves resolution (Unresolved -> StaticResolved) without orphaning any existing reference to the record. This deliberately diverges from TypeIdentity.canonical's own precedent (which DOES participate in its identity_key) -- judged as producing worse lineage-stability behavior for this specific case; TypeIdentity itself was left unchanged (out of scope).
call_model.extraction: adapter/src/semantic/rust/mod.rs: RustSemanticExtractor now walks function/method BODIES (previously only sig: &syn::Signature was ever inspected -- bodies were completely untouched through R4.4). New walk_block/walk_stmt/walk_expr recursively traverse Binary/Unary/If/Match/Block/Loop/While/ForLoop/Paren/Group/Reference/Field/Index/Return/Break/Assign/Try/Await/Struct/Array/Tuple/Closure/Cast/Range/Let (and Stmt::Local/Stmt::Item, the latter dispatching back through walk_item so a nested fn/struct/etc. declared inside a block is not call-walked as part of the outer function), finding syn::Expr::Call/MethodCall nodes and emitting one Call observation per site via a new emit_call() method, attributed to the enclosing function's FunctionIdentity record_id (computed independently of whether FUNCTION_IDENTITY itself was requested, so CALL attribution never silently disappears under a requested-dimension subset). A macro invocation (println!, todo!, ...) is parsed as syn::Expr::Macro/syn::Stmt::Macro, never syn::Expr::Call, so it is never mistaken for a call -- its expansion is not observable from syntax alone. CALL joins SUPPORTED_DIMENSIONS (now five: SYMBOL, TYPE, FUNCTION_IDENTITY, FUNCTION_SIGNATURE, CALL).
call_model.epistemic_discipline: Every CallSiteIdentity this extractor produces has dispatch=CallDispatchKind::Unresolved and callees=Vec::new(), with NO exception -- the extractor has zero use-import tracking and zero type inference, so it can soundly observe WHERE a call syntactically occurs and WHO makes it, but never WHOM it calls. No resolution heuristic (not even narrow same-file lexical matching) was implemented, judged too risky for producing false STATIC_RESOLVED claims given unmodeled shadowing/imports -- the maximally epistemically honest choice for this wave.
call_model.graph_projection: core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs: the previously no-op SemanticObservation::Call arm in add_typed_semantic_nodes() now creates one CallSite node per Call observation (identity = span 'path:line:column', attributes include dispatch) plus a MAKES_CALL edge from the caller's FunctionIdentity node -- never an edge to a callee, since callees are always empty this wave. The caller's graph node id is derived identically to how the FunctionIdentity arm derives its own node id (stable_id('node', 'function-identity:<record_id>')), confirmed byte-identical by tracing both derivations back through handle_function's shared identity.identity_key() computation, so the edge resolves correctly whether or not that FunctionIdentity observation is present in the same batch.

pipeline_losslessness.extractor_to_batch: walk_block/walk_stmt/walk_expr feed emit_call() -> ExtractionContext.observations, so every ExtractionBatch.observations entry for CALL carries the full CallSiteIdentity struct with evidence/provenance.
pipeline_losslessness.batch_to_census: build_census() required zero code changes to carry Call observations losslessly -- it operates generically over SemanticObservation, exactly as it did for R4.4's strengthened FunctionIdentity.
pipeline_losslessness.census_to_normalization: normalize()/normalize_typed_records() likewise required zero code changes; confirmed by a dedicated runtime multi-extractor round-trip test.
pipeline_losslessness.normalization_to_graph: add_typed_semantic_nodes()'s Call arm is the one place that DID require new code this wave (previously an explicit no-op) -- CallSite node + MAKES_CALL edge, proven by three dedicated graph tests.

multi_extractor_proof.claim: Two independent extractors reporting the identical Call claim (same repository/revision/function/span/dispatch/callees) both survive Census and Normalization as two independent typed_semantic_records entries.
multi_extractor_proof.mechanism: record_id() (built from CallSiteIdentity::identity_key(), which excludes dispatch/callees) is identical for both observations, proving the semantic CLAIM identity is unaffected by which extractor reported it; raw_observation_id() (extractor id/version + status + evidence_refs + provenance + full typed payload) differs between the two, so R4.3.3's raw_observation_id-keyed dedup (unmodified this wave) correctly keeps both.
